It covers a first bachelor's degree, a postgraduate diploma in the Faculty of Health Sciences, an honours degree or a coursework master's degree at UCT, but not part-time study or research-only degrees.

It is open to citizens of any African country applying for a first bachelor's degree or for an eligible UCT postgraduate diploma, honours degree or coursework master's programme, and UCT states that it encourages applications from young women, people living with disabilities, refugees and forcibly displaced youth.

Any costs not listed in the Mastercard Foundation's published coverage list (tuition, accommodation, books, mentoring, leadership development, return air ticket if necessary) are not confirmed as covered

UCT's only logo asset on its own domain, https://uct.ac.za/themes/custom/blip_uct/logo.svg (probed, HTTP 200 image/svg+xml), is a WHITE-ON-TRANSPARENT wordmark: every text path in the file is fill="#FFFFFF" and only the crest base is fill="#009ADA". new_scholarship.name: E-JUST TICAD8 African Scholarships for Science, Technology and Innovation
new_scholarship.program_type: Government-funded full scholarship for African nationals, delivered by a national university
new_scholarship.official_source: Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology (E-JUST)
new_scholarship.application_period: Published cycle on the E-JUST site is the Fall 2026 semester, with application submission closing 15 February 2026; the next equivalent cycle has not yet been published as of 2026-10-04.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Researchers or instructors (or those expected to become such) who need an M.Sc. in science or engineering or another specialisation, who hold the nationality of an African country other than Egypt and whose current home address is in an African country. Applicants must fulfil all E-JUST admission requirements and pass the academic interview and oral examination. Applicants who will continue in their jobs at their home universities or institutions after completing the programme are preferred, and in that case endorsement of the application by the home institution is required.
eligibility: Holder of the nationality of a country in Africa except Egypt
Current home address in an African country
Researcher or instructor, or a person expected to become one, needing an M.Sc. in a science or engineering field or other specialisation
Not serving in the military
Meets all E-JUST admission requirements and passes the academic interview and oral examination
coverage: International round-trip airfare from and to the applicant's home country
benefits: Six months of preparatory courses where necessary
requirements: Fulfil all E-JUST admission requirements
Pass the academic interview and oral examination
Equivalency certificate from the Egyptian Supreme Council of Universities and security clearance from the Ministry of Interior, both of which E-JUST applies for on behalf of successful candidates
Endorsement by the home institution where the applicant will return to work there
Full-time study only; scholarship holders may not work elsewhere during the scholarship period
required_documents: Online international admission application submitted through the E-JUST international admission tab
Academic documents required by E-JUST for the chosen programme
Endorsement of the application form by the home institution, for applicants who will return to it
Two recommendation letters or equivalent, as specified by E-JUST admissions
application_method: Submit the online application through the international admission tab on the E-JUST website
Sit the admission interview and oral examination as scheduled by E-JUST
new_scholarship.english_requirement: Full-time students: TOEFL iBT minimum 79 or Academic IELTS minimum 6.5. Provisionally accepted students: Duolingo English Test minimum 125, TOEFL iBT minimum 65 or Academic IELTS minimum 5.5, with a mandatory English language course in the preparatory year. Applicants whose native language is English, from countries where English is an official language, are exempt.
new_scholarship.selection_notes: E-JUST states that reasons for disqualification at any stage of selection will not be disclosed and that the schedule is subject to change. Academic background must match the programme's academic background tables. Support is conditional on good standing with the E-JUST graduate programme, and a semi-annual progress report is sent to the sponsor.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Academic staff and early-career researchers from African countries other than Egypt who need an M.Sc. in engineering, computer science, basic and applied sciences, international business and humanities, or heritage science, and who intend to return to their home institution.
new_scholarship.notes: Full-time award only: E-JUST states scholarship holders must devote themselves fully to study and research and are not allowed to work elsewhere during the scholarship period. Progress is reviewed semi-annually and reported to the sponsor. E-JUST states the scholarship term is the period needed to complete the degree requirements, normally two years for the M.Sc. plus six months of preparatory courses where necessary. The page read documents only the Fall 2026 cycle, whose submission deadline of 15 February 2026 has passed, so the record is treated as a recurring annual award whose next window E-JUST has not yet published.
new_scholarship.description: A fully funded master's scholarship offered by the Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology under the cooperation of the Egyptian government and the Japan International Cooperation Agency, for nationals of African countries other than Egypt. It covers tuition, accommodation, a monthly stipend, medical care and return airfare, and runs for the period needed to complete the M.Sc. degree requirements. Applicants who will return to employment at their home institution are preferred and must have their application endorsed by that institution.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: Fall 2026 intake published on the E-JUST site (submission closed 15 February 2026); the scholarship is an annual TICAD8 cycle and the Fall 2027 window had not been published as of 2026-10-04.

programme_detail_official.description: E-JUST offers TICAD8 African Scholarships for STI to develop high quality human resources in science, technology and innovation toward a future African STI network. These scholarships are provided under the cooperation of the Egyptian government and JICA, are fully funded, and are available to applicants who wish to pursue their M.Sc. degree in Engineering, Computer Science and Information Technology, Basic and Applied Sciences, International Business and Humanities, and Heritage Science programmes. Applicants must be nationals of an African country other than Egypt with a current home address in an African country.
programme_detail_official.program_type: Government-funded full scholarship for African nationals, delivered by a national university
programme_detail_official.coverage: Africa-wide, excluding Egypt: open to nationals of any African country other than Egypt who reside in an African country, studied in Egypt.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold the nationality of an African country other than Egypt and currently live in an African country, since both are named eligibility conditions
Have your home institution endorse your application form if you intend to return to work there - E-JUST states returning applicants are preferable but the endorsement is required in that case
Secure a language certificate meeting the published threshold, valid at the time of submission, or confirm your exemption
Align your academic background with the chosen programme's academic background table
Prepare for the interview and oral examination, where a minimum acceptance percentage of 60% is required
Plan for the Egyptian equivalency certificate and security clearance, which E-JUST applies for on your behalf after you pass the interview and oral examination
common_rejection_risks: Holding Egyptian nationality, which the eligibility wording excludes
Living outside an African country, since a current home address in an African country is required
A language certificate that has expired or scores below the published threshold, or missing the English exemption basis
Not passing the interview and oral examination; E-JUST states reasons for disqualification will not be disclosed
Not obtaining an equivalency certificate from the Egyptian Supreme Council of Universities or security clearance from the Ministry of Interior, which terminates the application
Planning to work outside E-JUST during the scholarship, which the full-time condition forbids
estimated_uncovered_costs: The monthly stipend amount is not published, so living-cost adequacy cannot be checked against official figures
No cap is published on the round-trip airfare covered
Nothing is stated about costs of obtaining the equivalency certificate and security clearance, which the applicant must acquire even though E-JUST applies for them
Fees for the six months of preparatory courses, if required, are not separately described

rejected.candidate: IsDB Scholarship Programs 2026-2027 (IsDB generic programme and its four component booklets)
rejected.reason: Strong theme fit but no verifiable current window. The four published programmes, including the IsDB-ISFD Scholarship Program for IsDB Least Developed Member Countries and the Master of Science Scholarship for IsDB Least Developed Member Countries, are genuinely targeted at low-income and least-developed countries, and the page lists African eligible countries for the Scholarship Program for Muslim Communities in Non-Member Countries. However the overview page carries stale body text stating that applications for the 2024-2025 academic year closed, the Scholarship Call for Applicants page renders with no substantive content, and the /scholarships/news page renders with no articles, so no open or forthcoming application window could be read from the awarding body.

Open and verified, but held back rather than written: eligibility is African nationality plus a master's degree and seven years' work experience, with only a neutral provision that the age limit is 45 for women with children. There is no need-based, gender, disability, displacement or fragile-state criterion, so it does not fit the targeted-need cell and would sit better with a regional or level cell.

rejected.candidate: SPARK Scholarship Program and Yemeni Pioneers Scholarship Program (both Türkiye Scholarships joint programmes)
rejected.reason: Deferred rather than written for this shard. Both are genuine targeted-need awards for the right populations, Syrian students under temporary protection and Yemeni students in a fragile state, and both are published under the awarding body's heading that joint scholarship programmes are 'offered to certain disadvantaged groups'. However the joint-programme page publishes no application window, no degree levels and no funding amounts for either, and the only Türkiye Scholarships application window published anywhere on the site is the General Application Period of 10 January to 20 February, which the brief warns must not be universalised from the parent programme to a specific joint programme. Held back rather than assert a window or level that the awarding body does not publish for them.

rejected.candidate: L'Oreal-UNESCO For Women in Science Young Talents programmes for Sub-Saharan Africa and the Arab States
rejected.reason: Best remaining women-in-STEM fit for the cell but no verifiable window. The Fondation L'Oréal page confirms the Sub-Saharan Africa programme spans the 48 Sub-Saharan African countries and offers 30 endowments from EUR 10,000 to EUR 15,000 to women at PhD and post-doctoral level, with Levant, Maghreb and Middle East regional programmes alongside Egypt and South Africa national ones, and applications run through forwomeninscience.com. But the page publishes no application dates, and the application map at https://www.forwomeninscience.com/map/ timed out. The word 'Open' printed beside every region heading on that page is a disclosure-widget toggle, appearing identically next to Europe, Asia and the Pacific and North America, and was deliberately not misread as an applications-open status. Separately the Fondation L'Oréal logo asset logo-black.svg was probed and rejected: its 'FONDATION L'OREAL' strapline paths use fill #CDC3C1, a pale warm grey far too light to read on a white card.
